title: World Bank EdStats: Public Expenditure Efficiency, Teacher Compensation Ratios, and Cognitive Attainment Benchmarks
description: Cross-country macro-level indicators examining government education expenditure as a percentage of GDP, pupil-teacher ratios, teacher salary relative to GDP per capita, and secondary mathematics proficiency attainment benchmarks.
observation_unit: Cross-national policy indicator panel tracking educational finance and student proficiency
sample_population_note: Annual harmonized World Bank EdStats dataset covering national educational systems
sample_population_size: Standardized World Bank / UNESCO cross-national indicators
title_ja: 【世界銀行EdStats】教育支出対GDP比率・教員給与水準・生徒教師比と学力習熟度の多変量分析

research_angles.title: The High-Efficiency Expenditure Paradox: Why Japanese Educational Attainment Outperforms Higher-Spending OECD Counterparts
research_questions: Does aggregate government spending as a percentage of GDP linearly predict student mathematics proficiency across OECD economies?
Do teacher compensation stability and low pupil-teacher ratios dominate over gross macro spending in explaining attainment?
hypotheses: Gross education expenditure (% GDP) demonstrates diminishing marginal returns on cognitive proficiency benchmarks beyond a baseline threshold.
Multiple regression confirms that teacher salary ratios and favorable pupil-teacher ratios explain variance with clean multicollinearity diagnostics (VIF < 2.0).
research_angles.theoretical_framework: Educational Production Function Theory (Hanushek) and Institutional Economic Model
